page: Amazon Web Services g6.xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, engineered for graphics virtualization and artificial intelligence workloads. The platform pairs a 3.4 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with a dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 22 GB of VRAM. Compute resources comprise 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 16 GB of DDR4 system RAM operating at 3 GHz. Local scratch space is bundled via an integrated 250 GB NVMe SSD, while network communication operates at a 2 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data reveals a strong division between GPU-accelerated pipelines and host CPU tasks. In AI inference evaluations, the NVIDIA L4 GPU registers top-tier performance, processing 2,295.65 prompt tokens per second and generating 53.52 tokens per second on 7B parameter models, with small 135M model prompt ingestion exceeding 12,160 tokens per second. Host-level single-core CPU metrics remain competitive, placing in the top quartile under stress-ng. However, aggregate multi-core throughput, software compilation, and large-block memory read bandwidth (32.96 GB/sec) reflect the constraints of its two-core physical footprint, showing below-average scores across multi-threaded CPU suites.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the g6.xlarge provides an economical entry point into modern Ada Lovelace hardware acceleration without requiring multi-GPU system overhead. The main operational tradeoffs involve the 4-vCPU ceiling and 2 Gbps baseline network speed, which may bottleneck complex data preprocessing or high-throughput distributed ingestion. The server is ideally deployed for small-to-medium large language model inference, AI-driven audio and video pipelines, remote 3D graphics rendering, and developer testbeds focused on accelerated machine learning workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.xlarge is an accelerated computing virtual machine tailored for graphics and artificial intelligence workloads. Operating under the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server combines a 4-vCPU AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with 16 GB of DDR4 memory and a dedicated 250 GB NVMe SSD. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU offering 22 GB of VRAM on the Ada Lovelace architecture. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier execution in language model prompt processing and generation for small to medium parameter models. While single-threaded host compute is strong, multi-core tasks, system memory throughput, and the 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth reflect its compact physical core allocation. The g6.xlarge operates as a balanced platform for low-to-medium parameter model inference, remote graphics rendering, video encoding, and AI development environments.
